title: Activation-conditioned quant orchestration and runtime microkernel handshake for stable INT8 inference
creator: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:
Build an activation-conditioned quantization orchestration that performs SmoothQuant-style per-tensor/per-channel activation scaling during calibration and exposes a lightweight runtime microkernel handshake so the serving runtime can select fused kernels (rescale+matmul/conv) or a compensated execution path with minimal latency impact. This ticket covers the orchestration, calibration harness updates, runtime ABI for kernel capability negotiation, and the validation/canary plan to ensure accuracy and latency SLOs are preserved.

Background and motivation:
- SmoothQuant-like techniques (activation-aware scaling) reduce post-training INT8 accuracy loss by redistributing dynamic range from activations to weights, but require coordinated calibration artifacts and runtime kernel support for fused rescale operations.
- Current calibration pipelines produce static per-layer scales but runtime lacks a standard handshake for choosing between a fused rescale kernel and a fallback path that applies scaling at runtime with KV-cache-aware optimizations.
- We need a production-ready flow: calibrate -> generate quant profiles (per-channel weight scales + activation rescale factors) -> ship profile with model -> runtime negotiates kernel capability -> use fused kernel when available, fallback otherwise, with telemetry and automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration harness can ingest a golden corpus and generate activation rescale profiles (per-layer, per-axis) for INT8 deployment; outputs packaged as a deterministic profile file (.rqd-profile) with checksum.
- Runtime exposes a microkernel capability/feature negotiation API in the model manifest so the serving node can indicate support for fused-rescale matmul/conv and an alternate compensated execution path.
- Implement a small fused-rescale microkernel shim on x86 CUDA and A100 paths (prototype) and a reference CPU fallback that preserves accuracy but may cost more compute.
- E2E accuracy regression on the golden corpus: delta <= 0.5% relative to FP16 baseline for representative LLMs (7B and 13B family) across top-1/token perplexity metrics used by eval harness.
- Latency impact at p50 <= +5% and p99 <= +20% compared to current INT8 runtime baseline (without rescale).
- CI gating: calibration profile + kernel candidate must pass golden-corpus regression and perf benchmarks before canary release.

Design notes (high level):
1) Calibration pipeline changes:
   - Add an activation-statistics collector stage in the existing int8-calib harness that computes per-layer activation max/percentile and per-channel weight stats.
   - Compute a rescale factor r_l for each layer such that scaled activation dynamic range fits weight quantization budget; algorithm mirrors SmoothQuant but supports alternative heuristics (L2 vs max, percentile-based clipping).
   - Produce a profile JSON containing: layer_id, op_type, rescale_axis, rescale_factor (float32), weight_scales (per-channel as float32 array), histogram seed checksum.
   - Include a reproducible seed and calibration corpus snapshot id; store provenance link to Confluence design doc and golden-corpus S3 folder.

2) Runtime microkernel handshake/ABI:
   - Extend model manifest with "kernel_capabilities" and "quant_profile_id" fields. Manifest example: kernel_capabilities:["fused_rescale_matmul_v1","rescale_compensated_path_v1"]
   - On model load, the runtime queries available accelerated kernels on the device; if fused_rescale kernel present, runtime binds the fused path; otherwise binds compensated path which performs scaled matmul + corrected bias application.
   - Ensure KV cache hotpath works with compensated path by testing incremental cache refill and ensuring prefix caching doesn't double-apply rescale.

3) Kernel implementation & fallbacks:
   - Prototype fused kernel for CUDA (A100) that applies per-channel weight scaling and activation rescale in the GEMM kernel to avoid extra memory passes.
   - Provide a thread-parallel fallback path that applies activation rescale into a temporary buffer and calls existing INT8 matmul kernel; optimization: fuse rescale into prefetch stage to keep memory bandwidth reasonable.
   - Microkernel shim registers capabilities and exposes a small perf hint API so runtime can request "high-accuracy" vs "low-latency" variants.

4) Telemetry & validation:
   - Emit telemetry at token-level for canaries: quant_profile_id, kernel_variant, p50/p99 latency, token perplexity on evaluation prompts, and top-k distribution drift metrics.
   - Hook Canary monitors to evaluate quality drift vs baseline and trigger automatic traffic rollback if accuracy regressions cross threshold (delta > 0.5% or BLEU/EM equivalent depending on eval).

Implementation plan (tasks):
- T1 (Calibration): update calib harness to compute rescale factors and produce profile files. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/quant/calb-design (design doc).
- T2 (Profile packaging): canonicalize profile file format, sign/profile checksum, store in model registry.
- T3 (Runtime manifest): add fields and negotiation logic for kernel capabilities.
- T4 (Microkernel): build prototype fused kernel for CUDA (A100), submit PR.
- T5 (Fallback): implement compensated runtime path and tests.
- T6 (CI & gating): integrate golden-corpus regression into pipeline, add perf benchmarks.
- T7 (Canary): canary rollout with telemetry dashboards and automated rollback.

Progress updates / comments:
- 2025-02-19 - Aisha Raman: Initial scoping and prototype algorithm sketched. Chose percentile-based clipping (99.999th) with optional L2 fallback when distribution noisy. Added golden-corpus list (s3://rw-golden-corpora/sq-v1).
- 2025-02-22 - Miguel Soto: Started calibration harness changes; wrote collector module and unit tests. Collector currently samples activation stats from 1000 sequences; need to scale to 10k for stable percentiles.
- 2025-02-25 - Review (PM - Clara Ng): PM requested explicit canary thresholds and SLO rollback policy; added to acceptance criteria. Also noted enterprise customers expect signed profile artifacts.
- 2025-02-27 - Design review notes: prefer deterministic profile serialization (sorted keys, stable arrays) to avoid tiny diffs across runs; decision approved.
- 2025-02-28 - Eng pairing (Miguel + Priya): prototyped kernel handshake in runtime manifest; stubbed kernel capability enumerator for CUDA devices.
- 2025-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/2921 (runtime manifest + negotiation).
- 2025-03-02 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib/pull/178 (calib harness + profile packaging).

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit tests for collector + deterministic profile serialization.
- Offline golden-corpus regression: run calibration -> quantize model -> run eval harness (100 eval prompts across 7B/13B variants) and assert metrics (see acceptance).
- Performance microbench: measure p50/p99 token generation for baseline INT8 vs fused-rescale vs compensated path across typical batch sizes and sequence lengths (8/512, 1/2048).
- Integration test for KV-cache: run long prefix sequences to check tokens generated match baseline and that cache hits maintain expected speedups.

Rollout strategy:
1) Internal opt-in experiment: expose kernel_capabilities flag in runtime to opt-in teams (console flag).
2) Canary 5% traffic on non-critical models with automatic monitoring for drift; increase to 25% after 48h of stable metrics.
3) Gradual platform rollout with per-customer opt-out for enterprise tenants until signed profile support validated.

Open questions / next decisions required:
- Q1: Which percentile/clipping strategy yields best accuracy/stability tradeoff for LLM families beyond 13B? (Action: run extended calibration across big-corpus by 2025-03-14).
- Q2: Should we include per-layer quantization bit-width suggestions in the same profile (e.g., mix FP8/INT8 hints) or keep profile focused solely on rescale factors? PM suggests separate mixing ticket.
- Q3: Operational signing: use KMS to sign profiles or embed registry-signed checksum? (Security ops consult needed).

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (drive): https://drive.redwood.com/quant/activation-handshake-design
- Golden corpus S3: s3://rw-golden-corpora/sq-v1
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/2921
- Calib PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib/pull/178
- Canary dashboard (grafana): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/quant/canary-sq

Blocking risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Fused kernel rollout on some GPU families may be delayed; mitigation: ensure compensated path correctness and reserve capacity for canary.
- Risk: Profile nondeterminism causing flicker in canary; mitigation: use deterministic serialization and include corpus snapshot id.
- Risk: KV cache double-scaling bug on compensated path; mitigation: add unit tests that exercise incremental cache apply and verify outputs against golden baseline.

Next steps (short-term):
- Miguel to land runtime manifest PR and add unit tests (ETA 2025-03-05).
- Priya to iterate on fused kernel prototype and benchmark (ETA 2025-03-12).
- QA to set up golden-corpus regression job and baseline (ETA 2025-03-10).

History & context pointers:

- This ticket consolidates orchestration, runtime ABI, and kernel handshake to avoid duplicated effort across multiple INT8 rollout attempts.

Acceptance checklist (to close):
- [ ] Calibration harness produces stable, signed profile files and stores in model registry.
- [ ] Runtime can negotiate kernel capability and select fused or compensated path without changed API for customers.
- [ ] Fused kernel prototype available with basic perf improvement on A100.
- [ ] Golden-corpus regression shows accuracy within thresholds.
- [ ] Canary rollout plan executed with automated rollback on drift.

Comments:
